p.text: What does Mr Karimov say belongs in minutes?
options: What was decided, by whom, and by when
The main argument of each speaker
A short summary and a list of names
The date and the place only

fb.correct: 'Minutes are past tense and no adjectives. What was decided, by whom, and by when.'
fb.incorrect_default: 'Minutes are past tense and no adjectives. What was decided, by whom, and by when.'

1.say: This is the last one I will read before I stop reading them. Then be hard on it. Paragraph two. What is it about? The bridge, and the cost, and the school year. Three paragraphs, then. One point each, and the point in the first line. The first line is where I like to build up to it. Build up to it in a story. In a report the reader may stop at any line, and you want them to stop after the point, not before it. The summary at the front is written last. It always is. A summary that was written first is a plan, and a plan is not what happened. And the minutes of the meeting? Kamola says mine read like a story. Minutes are past tense and no adjectives. What was decided, by whom, and by when. Nothing else belongs in them. Every kind of document has its own shape. And you now know four of them, which is three more than I had at your age. You will still read them, though. I will read them because I want to. That is a different thing, and it is the better half of the job.

grammar.label: the topic sentence and paragraph shape

explanation.en: An academic paragraph opens with the claim, supports it, and ends pointing at the next. A reader should be able to read only the first sentence of every paragraph and still follow the argument. If they cannot, the paragraph is carrying two points and should be split.
explanation.uz: Ilmiy xatboshi da'vo bilan boshlanadi, uni asoslaydi va keyingisiga bog'laydi. Har xatboshining birinchi gapini o'qib chiqib, fikr yo'nalishini tushunish mumkin bo'lishi kerak.

grammar.positive_example: Delay was the main cause. Three of the four reports arrived late, and the fourth was incomplete.
grammar.negative_example: Three of the four reports arrived late. The building was also cold. Delay was the main cause.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek va rus an'analarida xulosa ko'pincha oxirida keladi; ingliz ilmiy uslubida esa da'vo boshda turadi.

grammar.label: genre shape — abstract, minutes and executive summary
grammar.form: fixed section order and tense conventions per genre
grammar.meaning: each written genre has a shape the reader expects

explanation.en: An abstract runs background, aim, method, result, conclusion, in the past for what was done and the present for what it shows. Minutes record decisions and actions with an owner and a date, in the past. An executive summary states the recommendation first, because most readers stop there.
explanation.uz: Annotatsiya: fon, maqsad, usul, natija, xulosa. Bayonnoma: qarorlar, mas'ul shaxs va sana bilan. Qisqacha hisobot: tavsiya birinchi o'rinda, chunki ko'pchilik shu bilan cheklanadi.

grammar.positive_example: We recommend closing the annex. The evidence for this is set out below.
grammar.negative_example: The evidence is set out below, and a recommendation appears on the final page.

l1_notes.uz: Janr shakli o'rganiladigan konventsiya; uni bilmaslik matnni mazmunidan qat'i nazar notabiiy qiladi.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: This is the last one I will read before I stop reading them.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Paragraph two. What is it about?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The bridge, and the cost, and the school year.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Three paragraphs, then. One point each, and the point in the first line.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The first line is where I like to build up to it.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Build up to it in a story. In a report the reader may stop at any line, and you want them to stop after the point, not before it.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The summary at the front is written last.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: It always is. A summary that was written first is a plan, and a plan is not what happened.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: And the minutes of the meeting? Kamola says mine read like a story.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Minutes are past tense and no adjectives. What was decided, by whom, and by when. Nothing else belongs in them.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Every kind of document has its own shape.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: And you now know four of them, which is three more than I had at your age.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: You will still read them, though.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: I will read them because I want to. That is a different thing, and it is the better half of the job.
